newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends higher ahead of GCA stock data.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends higher ahead of GCA stock data.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended higher Friday, buoyed by expectations of a drawdown in monthly consumer stocks, market sources said.
Green Coffee Association stock figures for October, due out after 1500 EST today, are expected to show a decline of between 200,000 and 300,000 60-kg bags, traders said.
In September, supplies of green coffee in U.S. warehouses fell to 1,611,000 bags, their lowest level since the GCA began tracking inventories eight years ago.
With prompt inventories running low, speculators once again moved to hedge the risk of another sharp drawdown in consumer stocks, traders said.
"The market was really nervous today," one trader said. "Everyone was focusing on the stocks."

Most-active March ended 1.90 cents a lb higher, at 114.30, after ranging narrowly from 114.50 to 112.70. Spot December futures rose 0.90 cent a lb on the day, to 122.50. The remaining months finished 0.70 to 1.65 higher.

Despite near-term supply concerns, the closely watched December/March spread narrowed to 8.20 cents, down from 9.20 cents at Thurday's close, as operators continued adjust their books ahead of December's first notice day November 19.
As of Thursday, December's open interest stood at 4,461 lots -- the equivalent of more than one million bags of coffee.

Meanwhile, the CSCE reported earlier this week U.S. certified coffee stocks fell by 471 60-kg bags in the week ended Nov. 8 to 333 bags, the lowest level since the exchange started tracking inventories in 1980.
The CSCE will release its next certified stock report after the close of business on Monday.

On the charts, near-term March resistance was pegged at the 115.00-cent level, with the next upside hurdle seen at 117.50. Support was put near 108.40. In the December contract, resistance was seen at 124.50, and support was noted near 115.00.
The day's volume was moderate, at an estimated 7,049 lots.
